title: Teelaunch Review: Who It Fits and Who Should Skip It
excerpt: Teelaunch is a Shopify-native print-on-demand app with easy setup and a decent product range, but its catalog and integrations are limited. A fit assessment for which store profiles it serves well and which should look elsewhere.
body: Teelaunch is a Shopify-native print-on-demand app, and its whole personality follows from that. Setup is fast, the product range is respectable for everyday categories, and the app lives inside the Shopify admin instead of making you shuttle between systems. For a store that runs on Shopify and wants to test print-on-demand without a long onboarding, it is one of the easiest doors in. The question is not whether it works, but which store profiles it serves well.

The stores that fit Teelaunch best share three traits. They sell a small catalog of designs that they plan to test and rotate, they value a short setup time over the widest possible catalog, and they want most of the flow, from product sync to order fulfillment, to stay inside the Shopify app they already know. If those three are true, the app's simplicity is a feature, not a limitation.

The stores that should look further are the ones whose needs outgrow the app's edges. A store that sells into several marketplaces, or wants deep integrations with custom tools, or needs a catalog wider than the leaders offer, will feel the limits quickly. Limited integrations matter more the more channels you add, because every channel that cannot talk to the app becomes manual work. A multi-channel roadmap is a good reason to check the integration list before committing.

The cost side stays simple, which is part of the appeal. Teelaunch works on a free-plus-product-cost model, so there is no monthly platform fee to amortize; you pay the base product, the decoration work, and the per-order shipping, and your margin is the difference after the sale price. For a store testing new designs every week, that pay-as-you-go structure keeps the fixed costs near zero while you learn which products convert.

The practical way to decide is to run a two-week trial with your three best product ideas. Load the designs, order samples for yourself, and check three things: print quality on your fabric, production plus transit time to your top market, and how the app handles an order change or a return. Sample orders are the cheapest research you can buy, and they reveal what the catalog page never shows.

If the trial passes on quality, speed, and workflow, Teelaunch is a legitimate long-term partner for a Shopify-first store. If any of the three fails, the failure tells you what to look for elsewhere, which is a better outcome than discovering it after fifty orders.
